slides.title: Partition Of Unity
slides.notes: Open by framing the appendix as a compact tool that makes global differential geometry possible. The source span is only printed pages 272 through 274, but it supplies the mechanism used elsewhere to build metrics, connections, and extensions from local ingredients.

slides.title: The Problem It Solves
slides.notes: Emphasize the mismatch that partitions of unity repair. Local formulas are easy because charts, trivializations, and closed-set extensions live in neighborhoods. Global objects must agree everywhere. The partition assigns compatible weights so the local answers can be averaged without losing smoothness.

slides.title: Subordinate Partition
slides.notes: State the definition as three separate checks students can run. Each weight is smooth and nonnegative, each weight lives inside its assigned open set by support containment, and local finiteness makes the sum at a point a genuinely finite sum equal to one.

slides.title: Local Finiteness Is The Engine
slides.notes: Slow down on local finiteness because it is easy to treat as housekeeping. It is the analytic reason an indexed sum defines a smooth function. Near any point only finitely many terms survive, so differentiation passes through the sum without convergence arguments.

slides.title: Lemma 1: Make A Local Bump
slides.notes: Present the first lemma as the atomic move. Around a chosen point inside a chosen neighborhood, build a smooth function that is positive at the point and vanishes outside that neighborhood. Coordinates reduce the construction to a product of one-variable cutoff functions.

slides.title: Lemma 2: Protect A Compact Set
slides.notes: The second lemma upgrades a point bump to a compact-set shield. Cover the compact set by finitely many positive neighborhoods, add the corresponding bumps, and obtain one smooth function that remains positive on the compact set while still vanishing outside the chosen larger neighborhood.

slides.title: Lemma 3: Shrink The Cover
slides.notes: The third lemma supplies room for supports. Starting from a locally finite open cover, choose a locally finite refinement whose closed pieces sit inside the original open sets. This gap is what lets later functions be positive where needed and zero before they leak outside.

slides.title: The Existence Proof As A Pipeline
slides.notes: Now assemble the three lemmas into the theorem. Shrink the cover, place an intermediate open neighborhood, use the compact-set bump lemma to build raw functions, add them into a positive smooth denominator, and normalize each raw function by that denominator.

slides.title: Normalization Turns Weights Into Unity
slides.notes: The normalization step is the punchline. The raw functions already have the correct supports and cover every point positively, but their sum is not one. Dividing each raw function by the total preserves supports and forces the weights to add to one.

slides.title: Why Supports Stay Inside
slides.notes: Use the nested sets visually. The refined set marks where positivity is required, the intermediate set is where the raw function may live, and the original open set is the permitted support container. Local finiteness ensures this picture occurs only finitely often near each point.

slides.title: Theorem 2: Extend From A Closed Set
slides.notes: Shift from existence of weights to the first major application. A function defined on a closed subset is differentiable there when it has local smooth representatives. The theorem says paracompactness lets those local representatives be glued into a smooth function on the whole manifold.

slides.title: Extension Formula
slides.notes: Explain the formula as weighted consensus. On each small open set choose either a local representative near the closed subset or zero away from it. Multiplying by subordinate weights makes the expression local, and on the closed set all contributing representatives agree with the original function.

slides.title: Globalizing Differential-Geometric Data
slides.notes: Connect the appendix back to the course. The same gluing device builds Riemannian metrics from chartwise metrics, fibre metrics from trivializations, and connection forms from local choices. Partition weights convert local differential-geometric data into a coherent global object.

slides.title: A Concrete One-Dimensional Model
slides.notes: Give students a small mental model before the abstract theorem fades. Two overlapping intervals carry two raw bumps. Their normalized versions cross-fade smoothly across the overlap, so a local left formula and a local right formula can be blended without a seam.

slides.title: Common Failure Modes
slides.notes: Use the warning slide to separate necessary hypotheses from decorative assumptions. Without local finiteness, sums may stop being locally finite. Without support containment, local formulas may be used where they are undefined. Without positivity of the denominator, normalization breaks.

slides.title: Instructor Check
slides.notes: Ask learners to verify the construction rather than memorize it. They should be able to name the cover, the refined sets, the raw bump functions, the denominator, and the final weights, then explain why each object is smooth and has the required support.

slides.title: What To Carry Forward
slides.notes: Close by identifying the portable lesson. A partition of unity is a smooth weighted voting system controlled by open sets. It turns local existence into global existence on paracompact manifolds, which is why it quietly appears behind many constructions in differential geometry.
